name: Manny Pacquiao
role: Filipino boxer; congressman (2010-2016), senator (2016-2022), 2022 presidential candidate
summary: Former world boxing champion turned Philippine legislator and born-again evangelical. His documented positions center on religiously grounded social conservatism (against same-sex marriage and divorce), anti-corruption and poverty/housing themes, federalism, and a drug-war stance that moved from support to acknowledging possible extrajudicial killings. He has a thin legislative record and few stated positions on most economic and institutional questions.

decide-locally.rationale: Backed federalism in 2019 as 'an equalizer between the national and local government'; in December 2021 vowed to push a federal system if elected.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Said in 2021: 'I'm against same sex marriage', on religious grounds, while saying he does not condemn people; added that as president he would implement a law if one passed.

more-religion-public.rationale: Said in 2021 that religious leaders, especially evangelicals, would be part of his Cabinet and anti-corruption task force.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Made fighting corruption his top priority, alleged in 2021 corruption across every branch of government, and said God put him in office to clean the country of politicians' corrupt practices. 'Out of touch' part is not addressed.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: In 2022 said he would get justice for the relatives of drug-war victims and was open to ICC investigation provided Filipinos' rights are protected.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Principal Senate author of the law creating the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development (R.A. 11201) and campaigned on poverty and housing for the poor.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Said in 2022 he would invoke the US-Philippines Mutual Defense Treaty if bilateral talks with China failed and Filipino lives were at stake, treating the alliance as usable.

death-penalty.rationale: Backed restoring the death penalty in his August 2016 Senate speech, saying God allows it to punish wrongdoers, and filed bills. In November 2021 he said he was only holding his bill and not pushing it because he did not want innocent people put to death until the judicial system is fixed; recent position is conditional.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Said in December 2021 that he is against divorce because the Lord has united the couple; opposes legalising divorce, though he would not stop lawmakers from passing a bill. Statement is about fault requirement; his opposition is to divorce itself.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Reported as one of three senators who opposed passage of the SOGIE Equality Bill from 2016, though he says he supports the LGBTQ community.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: In his 2016 speech said when the government punishes it is not an individual act but 'approved by God'; not a general statement on the source of political authority.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: In 2022 he said security forces may have committed extrajudicial killings under the drug war, answered yes when asked if they occurred, and vowed justice for victims' relatives. Earlier (2016-18) he backed the campaign but opposed killings by abusive police.

close-ties-china.rationale: Criticised Duterte's soft line on China in 2021 and in 2022 said 'we would not be bullied', planning a peace panel with China while saying he would invoke the US mutual defense treaty if talks failed and 'we are friends to all nations'. Mixed.

notes: Death penalty: strongly in favour 2016-2018, then in November 2021 held his bill pending judicial reform. Drug war: supported as senator, in 2022 said extrajudicial killings may have occurred. Many topics (abortion, age of criminal responsibility, anti-terror vote, wage platform) were found only in pages that could not be opened, so left null.
